title: Worldliness
definition: The doctrine of Worldliness teaches that worldliness is loving the values, desires, pride, and systems that oppose God while still trying to appear spiritually safe.
summary: Worldliness names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. worldliness is loving the values, desires, pride, and systems that oppose God while still trying to appear spiritually safe. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Worldliness because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: worldliness is loving the values, desires, pride, and systems that oppose God while still trying to appear spiritually safe. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because it can slowly train the heart to admire what Christ died to rescue us from. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Examine what shapes your loves. Follow Christ in daily choices, entertainment, money, speech, and ambition, not only in public worship. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
